candidates.title: Hybrid Speculative Decoding in RAG: When Do the Pros Outweigh the Cons?
candidates.abstract: Speculative decoding emerged as a way to break the sequential autoregressive decoding of Large Language Models (LLMs), based on the idea that a lightweight model produces draft completions, to be efficiently verified in parallel by the actual LLM. Building on recent work where a hybrid speculative decoding strategy was proposed for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications, we thoroughly analyze what makes such hybrid work. Results show that higher token budgets work in favor of hybrid methods. Additionally, we find that the performance varies considerably over different benchmarks, and propose an approximate diagnostic to estimate the performance of such hybrid setup upfront. Finally, we show that the use of a prefix-tree implementation for variable-length n-gram matching is $1.4\times $ faster than reported alternatives. For reproducibility, we release our code, to our knowledge the first public tree-merging implementation for hybrid speculative decoding (github.com/Gianni-Van-de-Velde/hybrid-speculative-decoding).
candidates.reason: RAG向けハイブリッド投機的デコードが有効になる条件をトークン予算やベンチマーク差から分析し、事前に性能を見積もる診断法を提案する研究で、投機的デコードの適用判断という推論高速化の実務に直接貢献する。
